inline.s: Bound to the field of objects, thought and awareness turn along with it,
from the nothing and the supreme alike, the wisdom of evenness is born.
Discrimination’s own-nature has being; in dependent arising it is naught,
discrimination may grasp and receive, yet dependent arising is no discrimination.
The manifold branches are produced, but as illusion they do not stand,
those marks are manifold, and yet discrimination does not stand.
Those marks are the very fault, born all from the bondage of the mind,
discrimination knows nothing, yet discriminates dependent arising.
This very nature of discrimination is that dependent arising,
discrimination is of many kinds, yet it discriminates dependent arising.
Worldly truth and ultimate truth, and a third that is born without a cause,
discrimination speaks of worldly truth; when cut off, there is the sage’s realm.
As in the work of practice, within the One the many appear,
yet within it there is no plurality; such is the mark of discrimination.
As with the many film-veils, discrimination shows the many colors,
the film has color and no color; in arising it is not thus discerned.
As when refining genuine gold, far removed from every stain,
the sky is free of cloud and film; so has discrimination been made pure.
There is no nature of discrimination, and no such dependent arising,
assertion and repudiation alike are wholly ruined by discrimination.
If discrimination has no nature, yet there is a nature of arising,
then from no nature a nature comes, and existence is born of nonexistence.
Relying on discrimination, one obtains that dependent arising,
name and mark forever accompany, and give rise to discriminations.
When in the end it is not accomplished, one then crosses discrimination,
and thereafter knows the purity; this is called the ultimate truth.
Discrimination has twelve kinds; dependent arising has six,
self-awakened knowledge; between these there is no difference.
The five dharmas are the real; own-nature has three kinds,
the practitioner discriminates these, yet never oversteps the Suchness.
The marks and dependent arising; their names give rise to discrimination,
and those marks of discrimination are born from that dependent arising.
Awakened insight well observes: no conditions, no discrimination,
when accomplished there is no nature; how then does discrimination wake?
That discrimination own-nature establishes the two own-natures,
discrimination appears in many forms; purity is the sage’s realm.
Discrimination is as the colors in a painting; arising contrives discrimination,
if it were other than discrimination, it would follow the heterodox teachings.
Discrimination speaks of what is thought, born of the union of the views,
free of the two discriminations, thus is it accomplished.”

Mahamati the great bodhisattva again said to the Buddha: “World-Honored One, please teach the marks of the self-awakened sage-knowledge and of the One Vehicle. If you teach the marks of the self-awakened sage-knowledge and the One Vehicle, then I and the other bodhisattvas, being well awakened to the marks of the self-awakened sage-knowledge and the One Vehicle, shall understand the Buddha-Dharma without depending on another.”
The Buddha told Mahamati: “Listen well, listen well; think upon it well. I shall speak it for you.”
Mahamati said to the Buddha: “So be it; I receive your instruction.”

The Buddha told Mahamati: “The object known by the former sages, handed down from one to another, is that discrimination has no nature. The great bodhisattva, alone in a quiet place, contemplates with self-awakening, not depending on another, free from the discriminations of views, advancing ever upward, enters the ground of the Tathagata; this is called the mark of the self-awakened sage-knowledge. Mahamati, what is the mark of the One Vehicle? It is this: having attained the awareness of the One Vehicle path, I speak of the One Vehicle. How is the awareness of the One Vehicle path attained? It is this: what is grasped and the grasping, in the abode of reality, gives rise to no discrimination; this is called the awareness of the One Vehicle. Mahamati, the awareness of the One Vehicle is not to be attained by the heterodox, the shravakas, the pratyekabuddhas, the Brahma kings and the like, but only by the Tathagata. Because of this it is called the One Vehicle.”
Mahamati said to the Buddha: “World-Honored One, why does the World-Honored One speak of three vehicles, and not of the One Vehicle?”

The Buddha told Mahamati: “Because it is not the Dharma of self-parinirvana, I do not say that all shravakas and pratyekabuddhas are the One Vehicle. Since all shravakas and pratyekabuddhas are tamed by the Tathagata, given the expedient of tranquility, and so attain liberation, not by their own power, therefore I do not speak of the One Vehicle.

Moreover, Mahamati! Because the habit-energy of the karmic affliction-obstruction is not cut off, I do not say that all shravakas and pratyekabuddhas are the One Vehicle. Not realizing the non-self of dharmas, not leaving the death of the delimited, therefore I speak of three vehicles. Mahamati, those whose habit-energies of all the arising afflictions are cut off, and who realize the non-self of dharmas — when the habit-energies of all the arising afflictions are cut off, they do not taste the flavor of the bliss of samadhi as an entity, and realize the taint-free realm. Having realized it, they again enter the supreme taint-free realm beyond the world, fulfilling all the requisites, and shall attain the inconceivable self-mastery of the Tathagata’s Dharma-body.”
The vehicle of the devas and of Brahma, the vehicle of shravaka and pratyekabuddha,
the vehicle of the Buddhas and the Tathagatas; I speak of all these vehicles,
yet so long as the mind turns, all the vehicles are not ultimate.
If that mind is extinguished, there is no vehicle and no rider,
no vehicle is established; I call it the One Vehicle,
and to guide sentient beings, I distinguish and speak the several vehicles.
Liberation is of three kinds, along with the non-self of dharmas,
afflictions, wisdom and the like; liberation is far from them all.
As a plank of driftwood on the sea, forever turning with the waves,
so too the foolish shravakas, blown about by the wind of marks.
Their arising afflictions cease; the habitual folly of the defilements remains,
they taste the bliss of samadhi, and abide in the taint-free realm.
They have no final goal, and yet they do not fall back,
attaining the bodies of the samadhis, and for an eon still not awake.
As one who is drunk, when the wine subsides, then wakes,
so too when they awaken to dharmas, they attain the Buddha’s supreme body.”
The Lankavatara Sutra, Fascicle Three
The Heart of the Buddha’s Words, Part Three

At that time the World-Honored One said to Mahamati the great bodhisattva: “The general marks of the mind-made body and its discrimination, I shall now speak. Listen well, listen well; think upon it well.”

The Buddha told Mahamati: “There are three mind-made bodies. What are the three? They are: the mind-made body of the samadhi of bliss and right absorption; the mind-made body that realizes the own-nature of dharmas; and the mind-made body born together with all kinds, without acting. The practitioner, knowing the marks of successive advancement upon the grounds, attains these three bodies. Mahamati, what is the mind-made body of the samadhi of bliss and right absorption? It is this: because of the bliss of samadhi and right absorption on the third, fourth and fifth grounds, the various self-minds are stilled, abiding in the ocean of mind, where the marks of the rising waves of consciousness do not arise; knowing that the objects manifesting from one’s own mind have a nature and no-nature; this is called the mind-made body of the samadhi of bliss and right absorption. Mahamati, what is the mind-made body that realizes the own-nature of dharmas? It is this: upon the eighth ground, observing and realizing that dharmas, like illusion, are all without anything whatever, the body and mind are transformed, attaining the samadhi of illusion and the other samadhi-gates, with boundless marks, empowered by self-mastery and light, adorned like exquisite flowers, swift as the will, like illusion, dream, the moon in water and a mirror-image, neither made nor maker, like made and yet unmade, with all forms and their manifold members fully adorned, entering the great assemblies of all the Buddha-fields, because it penetrates the own-nature of dharmas; this is called the mind-made body that realizes the own-nature of dharmas. Mahamati, what is the mind-made body born together with all kinds, without acting? It is this: realizing all the Buddha-dharmas, and the mark of the bliss self-obtained; this is called the mind-made body born together with all kinds, without acting. Mahamati, observing and realizing these three marks of body, one should cultivate and learn them.”
Not my vehicle, not the Great Vehicle, not spoken, nor a word,
not a truth, not liberation, and not the realm of nothing.
But the Mahayana, self-mastery of samadhi,
the various mind-made bodies, freely adorned with flowers.”

At that time Mahamati the great bodhisattva said to the Buddha: “World-Honored One, as the World-Honored One has declared, if a man or a woman commits the five inexpiable acts, he does not fall into the Avici hell. World-Honored One, how is it that a man or a woman who commits the five inexpiable acts does not fall into the Avici hell?”

The Buddha told Mahamati: “What are the five inexpiable acts? They are: the killing of father and mother, the injuring of the arhat, the disrupting of the assembly of monks, and, with an evil mind, the causing of the Buddha’s body to bleed. Mahamati, what is the mother of beings? It is the craving of thirst that renews birth, accompanied by greed and joy; as a mother stands upon the cause of birth. Ignorance is the father. From these one is born into the village of the six sense-fields; cutting off these two roots is called injuring father and mother. When those defilements do not appear, like the poison of a rat breaking out, and are cut off in the ultimate, this is called injuring the arhat. What is disrupting the sangha? The aggregates of differing marks gathered and accumulated, cut off in the ultimate; this is called disrupting the sangha. Mahamati, not realizing the self-common marks of external objects, and the body of the seven consciousnesses as the measure of one’s own mind, with the taint-free evil-thought of the three liberations, cutting off in the ultimate that sevenfold consciousness-Buddha; this is called, with an evil mind, causing the Buddha’s body to bleed. If a man or a woman commits these inexpiable deeds, they are called the five inexpiable matters, and are also called the five inexpiable acts.

Moreover, Mahamati, there are the outward inexpiable acts; I shall now expound them. When you and the other great bodhisattvas have heard this meaning, in ages to come you will not fall into ignorance. What are the five inexpiable acts? They are those inexpiable acts spoken of before. If one commits them, among the three liberations he does not at all attain the equal Dharmas of no-interruption. Apart from this Dharma, the rest are the transformation-powers that manifest the equal no-interruption: namely, the transformation-power of the shravakas, the transformation-power of the bodhisattvas, and the transformation-power of the Tathagatas, which, for the sake of those who commit the inexpiable acts, to remove their doubt and remorse and to exhort them, work by power and transformation, manifesting the equal no-interruption. No one who has committed the inexpiable deed throughout attains the equal Dharma of no-interruption, apart from realizing the measure of the self-manifestations of their own mind, free from the discriminations of body and possessions, free from the grasping of self and mine. Sometimes, meeting a good teacher, one is liberated from the continuous discriminations of other realms.”
Craving and love are called the mother; ignorance is the father,
the consciousness of the perceived realm is the Buddha; the defilements are the arhat,
the gathering of the aggregates is the sangha; in unbroken sequence cut off,
these are called the five inexpiable acts, which do not enter the Avici prison.”

At that time Mahamati the great bodhisattva again said to the Buddha: “World-Honored One, please teach the Buddha’s knowledge and perception. World-Honored One, what is the Buddha’s knowledge and perception?”

The Buddha told Mahamati: “Realizing the non-self of persons and of dharmas, knowing the two obstructions, free from the two deaths, cutting off the two afflictions; this is called the Buddha’s knowledge and perception. Shravakas and pratyekabuddhas who attain this Dharma are also called Buddhas. Because of this reason, I speak of the One Vehicle.”
Well knowing the two non-selves, the two obstructions and afflictions cut off,
forever free of the two deaths; this is called the Buddha’s knowledge.”

At that time Mahamati said to the Buddha: “World-Honored One, why does the World-Honored One, in the midst of the great assembly, proclaim such words as these: ‘I am all the past Buddhas, and of many and various births; at that time I was the wheel-turning sage-king Mandhata, the six-tusked elephant, the parrot, Shakra, the seer of the good eye, and so forth, through hundreds of thousands of births, as the sutras relate?’” The Buddha told Mahamati: “Because of the four equalities, the Tathagata, Arhat, and perfect Buddha, in the midst of the great assembly, proclaim such words: ‘At that time I was Krakucchanda, Kanakamuni, and Kashyapa Buddha.’ What are the four equalities? The equality of words, the equality of speech, the equality of Dharma, and the equality of body; these are called the four equalities. Because of these four equalities, the Tathagata, Arhat, and perfect Buddha, in the midst of the great assembly, proclaim such words. What is the equality of words? If by a word I am called a Buddha, that same word is also given to all the Buddhas; the own-nature of that word has no difference; this is called the equality of words. What is the equality of speech? It is this: my sixty-four kinds of Brahman-voice and speech-marks arise; those Tathagatas, Arhats, and perfect Buddhas likewise have such sixty-four kinds of Brahman-voice and speech-marks, without increase or decrease, without difference, the voice-nature of the kalavinka. What is the equality of body? It is this: my Dharma-body and form-body, with their marks and excellence, have no difference from those of the Buddhas, except that to tame the beings of the various different destinies, they display various different form-bodies; this is called the equality of body. What is the equality of Dharma? It is this: I and those Buddhas obtain the thirty-seven factors of bodhi; in brief, the Buddha-Dharma is the unobstructed wisdom; this is called the four equalities. Therefore the Tathagata, Arhat, and perfect Buddha, in the midst of the great assembly, proclaim such words.”
Kashyapa, Krakucchanda, and Kanakamuni are I,
because of these four equalities, I declare it to the Buddha’s children.”

Mahamati again said to the Buddha: “As the World-Honored One has declared: ‘I attained the most perfect enlightenment on a certain night, and on a certain night entered parinirvana; in between, not a single word was spoken, nor has been spoken, nor will be spoken; that which is not spoken, this is said to be spoken by the Buddha.’”
Mahamati said to the Buddha: “World-Honored One, for what reason does the Tathagata, Arhat, and perfect Buddha say: ‘that which is not spoken is spoken by the Buddha’?”

The Buddha told Mahamati: “Because of two dharmas I speak thus. What are the two? They are the Dharma self-obtained, and the abiding Dharma; these are called the two dharmas. Because of these two dharmas I speak thus. What is the Dharma self-obtained? What the Tathagata has obtained, I have also obtained, without increase or decrease. The ultimate realm of the self-obtained Dharma, free from the discriminations of words, free from the two courses of words. What is the abiding Dharma? It is the ancient path of the former sages. Like the nature of gold and silver, the Dharma-realm abides forever; whether the Tathagata appears in the world or not, the Dharma-realm abides forever. As one approaches that attained way, for instance, a man walking in the wilderness sees the even, true road to an ancient city, and straightway enters the city, enjoying the bliss of its delights. Mahamati, what do you think? Did that man make that road and the various delights of the city?”
He answered: “No.”

The Buddha told Mahamati: “The Dharma-realm of me and of all the past Buddhas abides forever, just so. Therefore it is said: ‘I attained the most perfect enlightenment on a certain night, and on a certain night entered parinirvana; in between, not a single word was spoken, nor has been, nor will be.’”
On a certain night I attained the way; on a certain night I entered nirvana,
between these two, I had nothing at all to say.
Because of the self-obtained and abiding Dharma, I speak thus,
that Buddha and I are wholly without difference.”

At that time Mahamati the great bodhisattva again requested the World-Honored One: “Please teach the marks of the existence and non-existence of all dharmas, so that I and the other great bodhisattvas, freed from the marks of existence and non-existence, may quickly attain anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.”

The Buddha told Mahamati: “The world relies on two kinds: namely, on existence and on non-existence; and falls into the desire to see the nature and non-nature, without leaving the marks of separation. Mahamati, what is the world’s reliance on existence? It is that existence is born of the causes and conditions of the world, not non-existence; born from existence, not from non-existence. Mahamati, one who speaks thus is saying that the world has no cause. Mahamati, what is the world’s reliance on non-existence? Having grasped the nature of greed, hatred and delusion, one then discriminates and grasps the nature of greed, hatred and delusion as non-nature. Mahamati, if one does not grasp the nature of existence, the marks of nature are still. Therefore the Tathagatas, the shravakas and the pratyekabuddhas do not grasp the nature of greed, hatred and delusion as existent or non-existent. Mahamati, what here is the ruiner?”
Mahamati said to the Buddha: “World-Honored One, it is when one grasps the nature of greed, hatred and delusion, and thereafter does not again grasp it.”

The Buddha told Mahamati: “Well said, well said. You understand thus. Mahamati, it is not only the non-nature of greed, hatred and delusion that is the ruiner; for the shravakas, the pratyekabuddhas, and the Buddha too, it is also a ruiner. Why is it so? Because inner and outer are unattainable, and because the nature of the afflictions is both different and not different. Mahamati, greed, hatred and delusion are unattainable whether inner or outer; because the nature of greed, hatred and delusion has no body and no grasping, the Buddha, the shravakas and the pratyekabuddhas are not the ruiners. Because the Buddha, the shravakas and the pratyekabuddhas are self-liberated by nature, since bondage and the cause of bondage are of no nature. Mahamati, if there is a bound one, there must be bondage as its cause. Mahamati, one who speaks thus is a ruiner; this is called the mark of the all-less. Mahamati, because of this, I say that one had better grasp the view of self as great as Mount Sumeru than to give rise to the prideful empty view of the all-less. Mahamati, those prideful in the all-less are called ruiners. Falling into the hope of self-common marks, not knowing the measure of the self-manifestations of one’s own mind; seeing outer natures as impermanent, destroyed in an instant and turning onward; the aggregates, realms and bases continuously flowing and changing, gone forever from the discriminations of the marks of words; this is called the ruiner.”
Existence and non-existence are the two extremes; even to the sphere of the mind,
purify that sphere, and the mind of evenness is stilled.
Not grasping the nature of the realm, extinction is not an all-less,
whatever is, is the Suchness, even as the sages’ realm.
Without a seed yet born, born and then again destroyed,
causes and conditions are existent and non-existent; they abide not in my teaching.
Not of the heterodox, not of the Buddha; not self, and not another,
gathered by causes and conditions, how can it be nothing at all?
Who gathers causes and conditions into existence, and then speaks of non-existence?
The heterodox discourse of the birth of dharmas, discriminating existence and non-existence.
If one knows that nothing is born, and likewise nothing is destroyed,
observing all this as utterly empty and still, both existence and non-existence are left behind.”

At that time Mahamati the great bodhisattva again said to the Buddha: “World-Honored One, please teach, for me and the bodhisattvas, the marks of the matter-awakening and the principle-understanding. If we are well able to discriminate the marks of the matter-awakening and the principle-understanding, then I and the bodhisattvas shall penetrate these marks, and having penetrated them, quickly accomplish anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, without following the discriminations of perception and the host of demons and the heterodox.”

The Buddha told Mahamati: “All shravakas, pratyekabuddhas and bodhisattvas have two kinds of penetration-marks, namely the matter-awakening and the word-awakening. Mahamati, the matter-awakening is this: relying on the mark of the self-obtained supreme advancement, far from the discriminations of words and letters, going to the taint-free realm, the self-mark of self-awakening, far from all false perceptions and discriminative thought, subduing all the heterodox and the hosts of demons, relying on the realm of self-awakening, luminous and blooming. This is called the mark of the matter-awakening. What is the mark of the word-awakening? It is the teaching of the nine-limbed and various discourses, free from the marks of different and not different, of existence and non-existence, and with skillful means, in accord with sentient beings, teaching the Dharma as is fitting, so that they attain deliverance. This is called the mark of the word-awakening. Mahamati, you and the other bodhisattvas should cultivate and learn it.”
The marks of the matter-awakening and the word-awakening, the self-obtained and the teaching,
if one sees them well discriminated, he does not follow the perceptions.
There is no true reality, as the foolish discriminate,
how can the thought of desire arise, taking non-nature as liberation?
Observing the conditioned, birth and death and their continuity,
one increases the two views, inverted and knowing nothing.
The One is the true truth; no guilt is nirvana,
observing the world’s discriminations as illusion, dream, and the plantain.
Though greed, hatred and delusion exist, yet truly there is no person,
from craving the aggregates are born; all that exists is like illusion and dream.”

At that time Mahamati the great bodhisattva said to the Buddha: “World-Honored One, please teach the marks of untrue discrimination. How does untrue discrimination arise? What dharmas are called untrue discrimination? In what dharmas is there untrue discrimination?”

The Buddha told Mahamati: “Well said, well said. You are able to ask the Tathagata such a meaning, of much benefit, of much happiness, pitying the world and all the devas and men. Listen well, listen well; think upon it well. I shall speak it for you.”

The Buddha told Mahamati: “Of the various meanings, various untrue discriminations grasp and so arise. Mahamati, the grasping of the grasped and the grasper, not knowing the measure of the self-manifestations of one’s own mind, and falling into the views of existence and non-existence, increases the heterodox views. The habit-energy of discrimination grasps the various external meanings. The discriminations of mind and the mental factors grasp and give rise to self and mine.”

Mahamati said to the Buddha: “World-Honored One, if the various meanings and the various untrue discriminations grasp and so arise; the grasping of the grasped and the grasper, not knowing the measure of the self-manifestations of one’s own mind, falling into the views of existence and non-existence, increasing the heterodox views; the habit-energy of discrimination grasping the various external meanings; the discriminations of mind and the mental factors giving rise to the grasping of self and mine. World-Honored One, if thus the various external marks of meaning fall into the marks of existence and non-existence, free from nature and non-nature, free from the marks of views — World-Honored One, the ultimate truth is likewise so, free from measure, limit, simile, cause and mark. World-Honored One, why then in one place does the discrimination of the non-real meaning, grasping the various natures, arise, and not a discrimination that grasps the marks of the ultimate truth? Is it not that the World-Honored One speaks a doctrine of wrong cause, speaking the one-born and the one-not-born?”

The Buddha told Mahamati: “It is not that discrimination is one born and one not born. Why? Because the discriminations of existence and non-existence do not arise. The external manifestation is of a nature that is non-nature; having realized the measure of the self-manifestations of one’s own mind, discrimination does not arise. Mahamati, I speak of the various discriminations of the foolish man’s own mind; when the various activities are before them, the discriminations of various natures and marks grasp and arise. How does the foolish man become free from the views of grasping self and mine? Free from the faults of the done and the doer, of cause and condition, having realized the measure of one’s own mind-discrimination, the body and mind are transformed, ultimately and clearly understanding all the grounds, the realm of the Tathagata’s self-awakening, free from the discriminations of the marks of the five dharmas, natures and things. Because of this reason, I say that discrimination arises from the grasping of the various non-real meanings. Knowing the real meaning, one attains liberation and stills the various discriminations.”
The various causes and conditions; from these the world is born,
discrimination grasps the four propositions, not knowing my penetration.
The world is not born from existence, nor is it born from non-existence,
not from existence and non-existence, and not not-from existence and non-existence.
The various causes and conditions; how do the foolish discriminate
that it is neither existent nor non-existent, nor again existence and non-existence?
Thus observing the world, the mind turns and attains selflessness,
no nature at all is born, because it is born from conditions.
All is made by conditions; the made is not self-existent,
a thing does not beget itself, because of the fault of the two things.
Without the fault of the two things, no nature of existence is obtainable.
Observing all the conditioned dharmas, free from the grasped and the grasper,
the measure of mind without a mind, I call it the measure of mind.
The measured is in the place of self-nature; the natures of the two are both left behind,
the nature ultimately wonderfully pure; I call this the measure.
The worldly self is a convention, but there is no real thing,
the aggregates and the convention of the aggregates, without a real thing, are likewise so.
There are four kinds of equality: marks and the nature of causes born,
the third, selflessness and the like; the fourth, the cultivating and the cultivated.
The habit-energy of discrimination turns, giving rise to the various minds,
the realms appear as external; this is the worldly measure of mind.
Appearing externally yet not real, the mind sees them as various,
establishing the body and possessions; I call this the measure of mind.
Free from all the views, and free from the thought and what is thought,
no attainment and no birth; I call this the measure of mind.
Not nature, not non-nature; nature and non-nature wholly left behind,
this is the mind’s liberation; I call this the measure of mind.
Suchness and the limit of emptiness, nirvana and the Dharma-realm,
the various mind-made bodies; I call this the measure of mind.”

At that time Mahamati the great bodhisattva said to the Buddha: “World-Honored One, as the World-Honored One has declared, a great bodhisattva should be good at meaning and words. What is it for a bodhisattva to be good at meaning and words? What are words? What is meaning?”

The Buddha told Mahamati: “What are words? The discrimination of words and letters combined, depending on throat, palate, lips, tongue, teeth, gums and cheeks, and because of my speech and another’s, the habit-energy of discrimination grasps and arises. This is called words. Mahamati, what is meaning? Being free from all the marks of discrimination and the marks of speech; this is called meaning. Mahamati, a great bodhisattva, in such meaning, alone in a quiet place, with the wisdom of hearing, reflecting and cultivating, relying on self-awakening, goes toward the city of nirvana; the habit-energy body having transformed, he realizes the self-awakened realm, and observes the marks of advancement in meaning between the grounds and the grounds. This is called the great bodhisattva’s goodness in meaning.”

Moreover, Mahamati, the bodhisattva good at meaning and words observes that words and meaning are neither different nor not different; and observes that meaning and words are likewise so. If words differed from meaning, one would not, by means of words, distinguish meaning; but one enters meaning by means of words, as a lamp illuminating forms. Moreover, Mahamati, the unborn and the unceasing, the self-nature of nirvana, the three vehicles and the one vehicle, the self-nature of the mind and so forth — if one grasps these by relying on spoken words, one falls into the views of assertion and repudiation. Different assertion, different discrimination, like the manifold illusions appearing. For instance, the various illusions — the common, deluded beings make different discriminations of them, but these are not the sages.”
That word being already discrimination, establishing the various dharmas,
because of that establishment, one dies and falls into the hells.
In the aggregates there is no self; the aggregates are not the self,
not as that discrimination, and again not non-self.
All things have existence, as the foolish discriminate,
if it were as they see it, then all things should be seen as true.
All dharmas have no nature; pure and impure both are naught,
not real, as they see it, and again not the all-less.

Moreover, Mahamati, the marks of knowledge and consciousness, I shall now speak. If you are well able to discriminate the marks of knowledge and consciousness, then you and the bodhisattvas will penetrate the marks of knowledge and consciousness, and quickly accomplish anuttara-samyak-sambodhi. Mahamati, that knowledge is of three kinds: the worldly, the supramundane, and the supreme supramundane. What is the worldly knowledge? All the heterodox and the worldly, grasping existence and non-existence. What is the supramundane knowledge? All the shravakas and pratyekabuddhas, falling into the hope and grasping of the self-common marks. What is the supreme supramundane knowledge? The Buddhas and bodhisattvas observe the Dharma of the all-less, see the unborn and the unceasing, free from the categories of existence and non-existence, enter the ground of the Tathagata, the non-self of persons and dharmas, born from the self-obtained. Mahamati, what is born and destroyed is consciousness; the unborn and unceasing is knowledge. Moreover, falling into mark and no-mark, and falling into the causal marks of the various existences and non-existences, is consciousness; going beyond the marks of existence and non-existence is knowledge. Moreover, the growing nature is consciousness; the non-growing nature is knowledge. Moreover, there are three kinds of knowledge: knowing birth and death, knowing the self-common marks, and knowing the unborn and the unceasing. Moreover, the unobstructed mark is knowledge; the mark of the various obstructions of realms is consciousness. Moreover, the mark of the expedient born of the union of the three things is consciousness; the mark of the non-expedient self-nature is knowledge. Moreover, the mark of attainment is consciousness; the mark of non-attainment is knowledge. The self-obtained realm of the sage-knowledge, neither going out nor coming in, is therefore like the moon in the water.”
